gaps.concept: Parathyroid chief cells secrete PTH; elevated ionized calcium suppresses its release.
gaps.why_tested: A parathyroid histology image or calcium challenge asks which cells and feedback response produce PTH.

gaps.concept: Primary hyperparathyroidism usually results from a solitary chief-cell adenoma: high calcium, low phosphate, and elevated or inappropriately normal PTH.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with incidental hypercalcemia must be distinguished from patients with suppressed PTH.

gaps.concept: Parathyroid adenoma shows a cellular, often encapsulated mass with little fat and a rim of compressed normal gland.
gaps.why_tested: A parathyroid specimen asks for the histologic diagnosis.

gaps.concept: MEN1-associated parathyroid hyperplasia often causes primary hyperparathyroidism and accompanies pituitary and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
gaps.why_tested: Hypercalcemia occurs alongside prolactinoma or a pancreatic endocrine tumor.

gaps.concept: MEN2A can cause parathyroid hyperplasia with medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma through activating RET mutations.
gaps.why_tested: A familial tumor syndrome includes hypercalcemia and asks for its genetic defect.

gaps.concept: Osteitis fibrosa cystica from excess PTH causes subperiosteal phalangeal resorption, a salt-and-pepper skull, and brown tumors.
gaps.why_tested: Skeletal imaging accompanies hypercalcemia and elevated PTH.

gaps.concept: Brown tumors contain fibrous tissue, osteoclast-like giant cells, and hemosiderin.
gaps.why_tested: A bone lesion biopsy accompanies biochemical hyperparathyroidism.

gaps.concept: Hypercalcemia causes nephrolithiasis, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric symptoms; ECG shows a shortened QT interval.
gaps.why_tested: A symptom cluster or ECG finding prompts recognition of elevated calcium.

gaps.concept: Chronic kidney disease causes secondary hyperparathyroidism through phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol: high PTH, high phosphate, low or normal calcium.
gaps.why_tested: Renal failure and bone disease require distinguishing secondary from primary hyperparathyroidism.

gaps.concept: Prolonged secondary hyperparathyroidism can become autonomous tertiary hyperparathyroidism, with elevated PTH and hypercalcemia despite persistent kidney disease.
gaps.why_tested: A dialysis or kidney-transplant patient develops hypercalcemia after longstanding high PTH.

gaps.concept: Renal osteodystrophy from sustained PTH excess may produce osteosclerosis of vertebral endplates, the rugger-jersey spine.
gaps.why_tested: Spinal imaging in chronic kidney disease asks for the underlying mineral disorder.

gaps.concept: Postsurgical hypoparathyroidism causes low PTH, low calcium, and high phosphate after thyroid or neck surgery.
gaps.why_tested: Tetany after thyroidectomy requires identifying the injured gland and expected laboratory pattern.

gaps.concept: AIRE-related autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 combines hypoparathyroidism, chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, and adrenal insufficiency.
gaps.why_tested: Childhood candidiasis and hypocalcemia point to an inherited autoimmune syndrome.

gaps.concept: Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A is maternally inherited GNAS-mediated PTH resistance: low calcium, high phosphate, high PTH, and Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.
gaps.why_tested: Hypocalcemia with elevated PTH and shortened fourth or fifth metacarpals distinguishes hormone resistance from gland failure.

gaps.concept: Paternally inherited GNAS defects cause pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism: Albright skeletal features without PTH resistance or abnormal calcium-phosphate labs.
gaps.why_tested: Similar skeletal findings in relatives but different laboratory patterns test genomic imprinting.

gaps.concept: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia results from inactivating CaSR mutations: lifelong mild hypercalcemia, low urinary calcium, and nonsuppressed PTH.
gaps.why_tested: Low urine calcium distinguishes this inherited condition from primary hyperparathyroidism.

gaps.concept: Activating CaSR mutations cause autosomal dominant hypocalcemia with low PTH and inappropriately high urinary calcium.
gaps.why_tested: Familial hypocalcemia with hypercalciuria asks for the opposite CaSR defect from familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.

gaps.concept: Severe magnesium deficiency can cause resistance to PTH as well as impaired PTH secretion.
gaps.why_tested: Hypocalcemia persists despite calcium replacement in a patient with marked hypomagnesemia.

gaps.concept: Tumor-secreted PTHrP causes high calcium, low phosphate, and suppressed endogenous PTH, classically with squamous cell carcinoma.
gaps.why_tested: Hypercalcemia in a patient with a solid tumor requires identifying the circulating mediator.

gaps.concept: Osteolytic malignancy, especially multiple myeloma, causes hypercalcemia through local bone destruction with suppressed PTH.
gaps.why_tested: Lytic lesions and hypercalcemia must be distinguished from PTHrP-mediated disease.

gaps.concept: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D reflects vitamin D stores; 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D may remain normal in deficiency because PTH stimulates activation.
gaps.why_tested: A suspected nutritional deficiency asks which vitamin D metabolite to measure.

gaps.concept: Vitamin D deficiency or malabsorption produces low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, secondary PTH elevation, low phosphate, and elevated alkaline phosphatase.
gaps.why_tested: Bone pain or deformity with a malabsorption history asks for the expected hormone and mineral pattern.

gaps.concept: Rickets is defective growth-plate mineralization: bowed legs, widened wrists, rachitic rosary, and metaphyseal widening, cupping, and fraying.
gaps.why_tested: A child with limb deformity has characteristic examination and radiograph findings.

gaps.concept: Adult osteomalacia causes unmineralized osteoid, bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, and Looser pseudofractures.
gaps.why_tested: An adult with fractures and low vitamin D must be distinguished from osteoporosis.

gaps.concept: Osteoporosis has reduced bone mass with normal mineralization and usually normal calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase.
gaps.why_tested: Fragility fractures with normal mineral studies distinguish osteoporosis from osteomalacia.

gaps.concept: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1A results from defective renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase: normal 25-hydroxyvitamin D but low calcitriol.
gaps.why_tested: A child with rickets and normal vitamin D stores has impaired activation.

gaps.concept: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 2 results from vitamin D receptor resistance, with high calcitriol and sometimes alopecia.
gaps.why_tested: Rickets with elevated active vitamin D and hair loss identifies receptor resistance.

gaps.concept: The vitamin D receptor is an intracellular nuclear receptor that regulates gene transcription.
gaps.why_tested: A receptor-mechanism question asks how calcitriol increases intestinal calcium transport proteins.

gaps.concept: Excess vitamin D causes hypercalcemia and hyperphosphatemia with suppressed PTH and possible nephrocalcinosis.
gaps.why_tested: Supplement use and elevated calcium plus phosphate distinguish vitamin D toxicity from primary hyperparathyroidism.

gaps.concept: Milk-alkali syndrome from excess calcium carbonate causes hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, and kidney injury.
gaps.why_tested: Heavy antacid use accompanies a distinctive calcium and acid-base pattern.

gaps.concept: Calcitonin is produced by thyroid parafollicular C cells derived from the ultimobranchial bodies.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology or thyroid histology image asks for the origin of calcitonin-secreting cells.

gaps.concept: Loss of PHEX function raises FGF23, causing renal phosphate wasting with normal calcium in X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets.
gaps.why_tested: Familial rickets with low phosphate but normal calcium asks for the genetic defect.

gaps.concept: Thiazides decrease urinary calcium and can raise serum calcium; loop diuretics increase urinary calcium.
gaps.why_tested: A diuretic exposure asks for the direction of calcium excretion or explains hypercalcemia.

gaps.concept: Lithium raises the calcium threshold for CaSR-mediated PTH suppression and can cause hyperparathyroidism.
gaps.why_tested: Hypercalcemia in a patient taking lithium asks for the drug’s effect on PTH regulation.

gaps.concept: Cinacalcet increases CaSR sensitivity to calcium, lowering PTH secretion in hyperparathyroidism.
gaps.why_tested: A drug-mechanism question describes treatment of elevated PTH in kidney disease.

gaps.concept: Denosumab blocks RANKL, preventing osteoclast formation and activity; hypocalcemia is a potential adverse effect.
gaps.why_tested: An antiresorptive monoclonal antibody is identified by its target or calcium effect.

gaps.concept: Bisphosphonates bind bone and inhibit osteoclast-mediated resorption; they are first-line drugs for most patients with osteoporosis.
gaps.why_tested: A fracture-prevention or hypercalcemia drug question asks for the antiresorptive mechanism.

gaps.concept: Bisphosphonates can cause esophagitis, osteonecrosis of the jaw, and atypical femoral fractures with prolonged use.
gaps.why_tested: A medication history accompanies dysphagia, a dental complication, or a subtrochanteric fracture.

gaps.concept: Rapid skeletal calcium uptake after parathyroidectomy can cause hungry bone syndrome and persistent postoperative hypocalcemia.
gaps.why_tested: Hypocalcemia after removal of a PTH-secreting adenoma requires a mechanism beyond gland injury.
